stem: If the frequency of a wave is doubled, then the time period of the wave will
explanation: The time period ($T$) and frequency ($f$) are inversely proportional to each other, given by the relation $T = \frac{1}{f}$. If the frequency is doubled ($2f$), the time period becomes $\frac{1}{2f}$, which is half of the original time period.

current_mapping.description: analyse key characteristics of waves by interpreting graphical representations of waveforms;

option_feedback.reason: Time period and frequency are reciprocals (T = 1/f), so doubling frequency halves the time period rather than doubling it.
Since T = 1/f, changing the frequency must inversely change the time period.
When frequency is doubled (2f), the new time period is T' = 1/(2f) = T/2 (half, not a quarter).

stem: If the time period of a simple pendulum is 2 s on the surface of the Earth, then the time period of the same pendulum on the surface of the Moon will be
explanation: The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$. Since the acceleration due to gravity on the Moon ($g_m$) is less than that on Earth ($g_e$) ($g_m \approx \frac{1}{6}g_e$), a smaller value of $g$ results in a larger time period $T$. Therefore, the time period on the Moon will be greater than 2 s.

current_mapping.description: solve word problems related to time period of a simple pendulum;

option_feedback.reason: Because g on the Moon is 1/6th of g on Earth and T = 2π√(L/g), a smaller g produces a longer time period (> 2 s).
Time period is inversely proportional to √g, so weaker gravity on the Moon increases (slows down) the oscillation period.
The Moon still has gravity (g_Moon ≈ 1.6 m/s²), so the pendulum oscillates with a period of 2 × √6 ≈ 4.9 s (> 2 s).

stem:
If a mechanical wave moves from a rare to the denser medium, then which of the following factors will change during refraction?
I. Wavelength
II. Speed of the wave
III. Frequency of the wave
explanation: During refraction, the frequency of a wave remains constant because it depends solely on the source. However, both the speed of the wave and its wavelength change when transitioning between media of different densities.

a. reflection,
b. refraction,
c. diffraction;

option_feedback.reason: When a wave crosses into a denser medium, its speed (I) changes, which also changes its wavelength (II) since λ = v/f.
Frequency (III) depends only on the vibrating source and remains constant when crossing between media.
Frequency (III) stays unchanged across the boundary; only wave speed (I) and wavelength (II) change.

stem: If an image is formed at a distance of 32 cm from a concave mirror with focal length of 12 cm, then the object’s distance is
explanation: Using the mirror formula: $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q}$. For a concave mirror, focal length $f = -12$ cm, and assuming real image $q = -32$ cm. Substituting values: $\frac{1}{-12} = \frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{-32} \implies \frac{1}{p} = -\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{32} = \frac{-8 + 3}{96} = \frac{-5}{96}$. Thus, $p = -\frac{96}{5} = -19.2$ cm.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between real and virtual images;

option_feedback.reason: –0.052 cm is the reciprocal 1/p before inverting to find p: 1/p = 1/f - 1/q = 1/(-12) - 1/32 (or with virtual image q = -32 cm, 1/p = 1/12 - 1/32 => p = 19.2 cm).
20.0 cm subtracts 32 - 12 instead of applying the spherical mirror equation 1/f = 1/p + 1/q.
32.0 cm is the given image distance q, not the object distance p.

explanation: Refractive index $n = \frac{\text{Real depth}}{\text{Apparent depth}}$. Therefore, $\text{Real depth} = n \times \text{Apparent depth} = 1.33 \times 3\text{ m} = 3.99\text{ m}$.

stem: Two capacitors of capacitance 6 µF and 3 µF are connected in a series across a cell of 18 V. The equivalent (effective) capacitance will be
explanation: For two capacitors connected in series, the equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ is given by $\frac{1}{C_{eq}} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1 + 2}{6} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$. Thus, $C_{eq} = 2\text{ \mu F}$.

option_feedback.reason: 3 µF is the capacitance of the smaller individual capacitor; in series, C_eq is always less than the smallest capacitor.
6 µF is the larger capacitor's value.
9 µF is the parallel sum (6 + 3), whereas in series 1/C_eq = 1/6 + 1/3 = 3/6 => C_eq = 2 µF.

stem: If the length and diametre of a solid cylindrical shape conductor is doubled, then the resistance will
explanation: Resistance $R = \rho \frac{L}{A} = \rho \frac{L}{\pi r^2} = \rho \frac{4L}{\pi d^2}$. If length $L$ is doubled ($2L$) and diameter $d$ is doubled ($2d$), then new resistance $R' = \rho \frac{2L}{\pi (2d)^2} = \rho \frac{2L}{4\pi d^2} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\rho \frac{L}{A}\right)$, which is half of the original resistance.

current_mapping.description: describe the phenomenon of superconductivity in solids;

option_feedback.reason: Doubling diameter quadruples area (A' = 4A), and doubling length (L' = 2L) gives R' = ρ(2L)/(4A) = R/2 (half, not a quarter).
Because cross-sectional area increases by 4× while length increases by only 2×, net resistance decreases to half.
Resistance is inversely proportional to area (πd²/4), so doubling diameter reduces resistance rather than increasing it.

Resistance is directly proportional to length (R = ρL/A), so the longer wire A has greater resistance.
A longer wire has greater resistance, not smaller resistance.

explanation: A transformer is a static electrical device that transfers electrical energy between two or more circuits through electromagnetic induction. It is primarily used to step up or step down alternating voltage or current.

option_feedback.reason: Protons (II) are positively charged and experience strong Coulomb repulsion from the +92e uranium nucleus.
Uncharged neutrons (I only) penetrate the nucleus without electrostatic repulsion to induce fission.
Electrons (III) are leptons that do not trigger nuclear fission in Uranium-238; only neutrons (I) induce fission.
